ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a battery labeled 12 volts, and the battery is connected by wires to the terminal board on the right. At the terminal board there is a resistor labeled 50 Ω, and next to it there is a Zener diode labeled Zener diode; the motor Motor is connected at the same controlled node/load end. Reasoning: According to the circuit shown, the 12 V power supply supplies the load node clamped by the 5 V Zener diode through the 50 Ω series resistor. Therefore the voltage across the series resistor is 12 V - 5 V = 7 V, and the resistor current I_R = 7 V / 50 Ω = 0.14 A = 140 mA. Given the motor current I_motor = 50 mA, by the node current relationship, the Zener current I_zener = I_R - I_motor = 140 mA - 50 mA = 90 mA. The Zener diode power dissipation P_zener = V_zener × I_zener = 5 V × 90 mA = 450 mW.

raw_record.question_text: Calculate the power dissipated by the 5-volt zener diode for the following values of motor current, assuming the battery voltage remains constant at 12 volts, as shown in the figure. Given \( I_\text{motor} = 50 \, mA \), the zener power \( P_\text{zener} \) is ______ mW.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify the 50 Ω resistor in series from the 12 V source to the regulated node, with the zener diode across the motor/load. From the text, take V_battery = 12 V, V_zener = 5 V, and I_motor = 50 mA. Since the zener clamps the load node at 5 V, the resistor has 12 - 5 = 7 V across it, so I_R = 7/50 = 0.14 A = 140 mA. By KCL, I_zener = I_R - I_motor = 140 mA - 50 mA = 90 mA. Then P_zener = V_zener I_zener = 5 V × 90 mA = 450 mW.

method.method_draft: From the image, note that after the 50 Ω dropping resistor the motor and zener are in parallel, so both are at the zener voltage. From the text, use V_source = 12 V, V_zener = 5 V, and I_motor = 50 mA. The series resistor current is set by the 7 V drop across 50 Ω: I_R = (12 - 5)/50 = 140 mA. Therefore the remaining power is dissipated by the zener: P_zener = 700 mW - 250 mW = 450 mW.
